builds.name: Reference: Mana scaling
builds.goal: Reference for Anivia: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A terrain-control mage who funnels enemies into a growing storm and capitalizes on chilled targets with Frostbite. Does chilled E damage or storm occupancy determine the fight? Compare real R growth, wall placement, mana exhaustion and opponents leaving the storm. Finite Rod stacks and a transformed mana item test later AP/mana-supported sequences.
builds.summary: Finite Rod stacks and a transformed mana item test later AP/mana-supported sequences.
testPlan: Kit question for Anivia: Does chilled E damage or storm occupancy determine the fight? Compare real R growth, wall placement, mana exhaustion and opponents leaving the storm.

Start with the early core (Rod early if the timer fits, then Archangel) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Finite Rod stacks and a transformed mana item test later AP/mana-supported sequences. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Anivia brings her wings together and summons a sphere of ice that flies towards her opponents, chilling and damaging anyone in its path. When the sphere explodes it does moderate damage in a radius, stunning anyone in the area. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Two delayed spikes can lose the game before full build; mana-to-AP values must be observed.
The route fails Anivia's stated kit question: Does chilled E damage or storm occupancy determine the fight? Compare real R growth, wall placement, mana exhaustion and opponents leaving the storm.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Two delayed spikes can lose the game before full build; mana-to-AP values must be observed.
Full cost 16,350 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Rod early if the timer fits, then Archangel. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

kitEvidence.formula:
Toggle: Anivia calls forth a driving rain of ice and hail that Slows enemies by [20 / 30 / 40]% and deals [30 / 45 / 60 + (0.125) × AP] magic damage per second. The storm increases in size over [1.5] seconds.

When the storm is fully formed, it Chills, Slows by [30 / 45 / 60]%, and does [(30 / 45 / 60 + (0.125) × AP) × (3)] magic damage per second instead.

Upon taking fatal damage, Anivia reverts to an egg, healing to full Health and receiving [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=-40, perLevel=0, changes=[{"mLevel": 5, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 8, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 12, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 15, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])] Armor and Magic Resist. If she survives for 6 seconds, she is reborn.

Anivia fires a massive chunk of ice, dealing [50 / 70 / 90 / 110 / 130 + (0.25) × AP] magic damage and Chilling enemies for [3] seconds, Slowing them by @Spell.GlacialStorm:SlowAmount@%. At the end of its range, the ice detonates, Stunning enemies for [1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5] seconds and dealing [60 / 95 / 130 / 165 / 200 + (0.45) × AP] magic damage.

Anivia can Recast this ability while the ice flies to detonate it early.

Anivia blasts an enemy with a freezing wind, dealing [55 / 80 / 105 / 130 / 155 + (0.55) × AP] magic damage. Against Chilled enemies, Anivia deals [(55 / 80 / 105 / 130 / 155 + (0.55) × AP) × (2)] magic damage instead.
Anivia summons a wall of ice [400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800] units wide. The wall lasts for [5] seconds before it melts.
